props.title: Four payoffs that justify the build

cards.head: Faster incidents
cards.body: Root cause in minutes, not hours — the RCA agent we build in part five.

cards.head: Safer changes
cards.body: Simulate blast radius before shipping — no more 2 a.m. surprises.

cards.head: Instant onboarding
cards.body: New engineers ask the graph how the system fits together — and get a real answer.

cards.head: Trustworthy AI
cards.body: A grounded world model is what lets an agent act without hallucinating.

props.foot: Every payoff here is something a stakeholder can feel — that's how the project gets funded.

props.kicker: WHY AGENTS NEED THIS · THE DECISION-CENTRIC ONTOLOGY
props.title: Palantir's insight: meaning isn't enough — model the action too

cards.head: Data
cards.body: The objects and links — your report, query, table, and how they relate.

cards.head: Logic
cards.body: Derived facts and business rules computed over the objects.

cards.head: Action
cards.body: The typed, allowed operations — ‘open a work item’, ‘page the owner’.

cards.head: Security
cards.body: Who — human or agent — may see and do what, enforced at the meaning layer.

props.foot: So: an ontology is the shared grammar — and it defines the safe verbs an agent is allowed to use.

props.title: Relationships are where relational databases hurt

left.head: SQL, many joins
rows: Queries get slow and unreadable fast.

right.head: Graph traversal
rows: A hop is just following an edge.
The query reads like the question.

props.foot: Relational is great for rows. Graphs win the moment the question is about connections.

props.title: The real skill: what you put in front of the model

cards.head: The subgraph
cards.body: Retrieve the small, relevant slice of the graph — not the whole thing, not random text.

cards.head: The schema
cards.body: Give the model the ontology so it grounds its terms and writes valid queries.

cards.head: Tools & memory
cards.body: Expose exactly the right MCP tools and recall past context — no more, no less.

props.foot: Prompt engineering grew up into context engineering — and the graph is your best context source.

props.title: Three loops worth knowing by name

cards.head: ReAct
cards.body: Reason, then act with a tool, then observe — and repeat. The workhorse loop.

cards.head: Plan-and-execute
cards.body: Draft a full plan first, then run the steps — better for complex, multi-tool tasks.

cards.head: Reflection
cards.body: The agent critiques its own output and retries — catching mistakes before you see them.

props.foot: LangGraph makes all three explicit as graphs of steps — pick the shape per task.

props.title: Three questions the living map answers for you

cards.head: “What breaks if…?”
cards.body: Impact analysis before any change — the cascade simulation from part three.

cards.head: “Why is this wrong?”
cards.body: Autonomous root cause across data, code, and logs — the traversal from part five.

cards.head: “How does this work?”
cards.body: A new hire asks the graph and gets the real architecture, not tribal knowledge.

props.foot: This is the ‘use it every day’ payoff: three threads of Slack become three answered questions.
